learning_objective: 🎯 Master the five components of health-related physical fitness, understand body composition, and learn how to develop a lifelong personal fitness plan!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Unlike skill-related fitness (which focuses on athletic performance like agility and speed), health-related fitness focuses on physical capabilities that prevent lifestyle diseases and improve daily functional health.

1) Cardiorespiratory Endurance (heart and lung efficiency), 2) Muscular Strength (maximum force exertion), 3) Muscular Endurance (repeated muscle contractions), 4) Flexibility (range of motion around joints), 5) Body Composition (ratio of fat to lean mass).

Body composition refers to the percentage of fat, bone, and muscle in the human body. Body Mass Index (BMI) is an initial screening tool used to categorize individuals as underweight, normal, overweight, or obese.
A scientifically proven framework for creating a workout routine: Frequency (how often), Intensity (how hard), Time (how long), and Type (what kind of exercise).

fun_activity.title: 🤸 The Sit-and-Reach Flexibility Check
fun_activity.instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you. Try to reach forward and touch your toes without bending your knees. Can you reach your toes comfortably, or do you need to work on your lower back and hamstring flexibility?

exam_tips: 📌 Do not confuse Health-Related Fitness (Endurance, Strength, Flexibility) with Skill-Related Fitness (Agility, Speed, Power, Balance).
📌 Be ready to calculate Body Mass Index using the formula: BMI = Weight in kg / (Height in meters)^2.
📌 Explain the F.I.T.T. principle clearly when asked how to design a personal fitness program.
quick_recap: ⭐ Muscular endurance is the ability of a muscle to perform repeated contractions over an extended period without fatigue.
⭐ Good flexibility reduces muscle soreness and lowers the risk of musculoskeletal injuries.
⭐ Aerobic exercises like swimming, running, and cycling are best for cardiorespiratory endurance.
